notes: PARTIAL (2026-11-16, the 1985 code reads, cause b: wrong the same way at every edition): the mechanism of kb/Work PB5729: PB5729 - a REDEFINES subordinate to the second or later record of a multi-record FD crashes the compiler with a .NET stack overflow in StorageFormPass.Classify (2002 and 2023). Owner: kb/Work PB5729 (open). Ruled in kb/Work/PB5683/2026-11-15-rulings-code-reads-batch-6.md; the 1985 rows that carry into this rule: 1985-GR-VII.4.4.4-6. Recorded by the registrar from the ruling and its note, the repro not re-run by the registrar. The prose that follows is the stored CONFORMS account, kept as the account of the part that holds. || kb/Work PB836 LANDED; kb/Work PB981 LANDED (determination D-FRA, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3). Sentence 1 - 'Multiple level 1 entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry represent implicit redefinitions of the same area': DataBinder.LinkImplicitRecordArea, the ONE linker for the FD and SD arms, joins every later CHARACTER-WINDOW level-1 record to the first through DataItem.SetRedefinition(first, RedefinitionKind.ImplicitFileRecord); the storage layout reads the one class for both constructs, while the 13.18.44.3 REDEFINES-clause screens read RedefinesKind == Clause only. Since PB981 a dynamic-length record, a variable-length group or a pointer-class record - legal source that used to be staged loud as COBOL0899 - is an OUT-OF-LINE record (FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord): 8.5.1.10.3 lets its storage be located elsewhere, so it is never linked into the class and shares the area at the transfer boundary instead - a READ/RETURN makes the current record available in it (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRecordAreaStore; a variable-length group through the one split rule CobolVarGroup.FromContiguous), and a WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE sends its contiguous image (8.5.1.11.2). The 2014 golden writes and reads back a variable-length group, a dynamic-length record and a character record of one FD, a SAME RECORD AREA peer and an SD; the 2002 golden a pointer record beside a character record. Residue stated in D-FRA: an EXTERNAL file whose area has an out-of-line record, and a SORT/MERGE key that follows a variable-length member, are refused by name. Sentence 2 - report description level-1 entries are not implicit redefinitions: the report binder never calls SetRedefinition. EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023 as before; the FD rule is COBOL-85 base language and the same binder arm serves 85. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#ClassifyRedefinesClasses (the pass body moved from the DataBinder partial to its own IBindPass class under Binding/Passes (kb/Work PB2352, PB2353, PB2354)) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#LinkImplicitRecordArea (kb/Work PB2296 M7 moved the member from DataBinder to FileControlBinder (the file binder); the same rule is asked by the same code) EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85, §1985:VI.5.7.4 GR3 'Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to any given level indicator other than the level indicator RD for a report description entry, represent implicit redefinitions of the same area' and §1985:XIII.3.14.4 GR2 'Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to a report description entry having the level indicator RD do not represent implicit redefinitions of the same area.'
